test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 23 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: If cosec 2θ = sec(θ - 30)°, then find the measure of θ (in degrees).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **complementary angles**, if **cosec A = sec B**, then **A + B = 90°**.

Here, A = 2θ and B = θ − 30°.

⇒ 2θ + θ − 30° = 90°

⇒ 3θ = 120° ⇒ θ = 40°.

**∴ The correct answer is 40°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** cosec 2θ = sec(θ − 30°)

**Formula Used:** cosec A = sec(90° − A)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c9bb69d6592fd27331463152ec4c8da01e814cd6e933dee0f39e9ececd3ac93a.png] 

⇒ sec(90° − 2θ) = sec(θ − 30°)

⇒ 90° − 2θ = θ − 30°

⇒ 90° + 30° = θ + 2θ

⇒ 120° = 3θ

⇒ θ = 120° ÷ 3

⇒ θ = 40°

**∴ The correct answer is 40°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angle Relations

Trigonometric ratios of complementary angles: sin θ = cos(90°−θ), tan θ = cot(90°−θ), and sec θ = cosec(90°−θ).

Identities for Co-functions

If f(A) = g(B) where f and g are co-functions (like sec and cosec), then A + B = 90° for acute angles.</p
